name: Gerchberg-Saxton benchmarking
description:
Due to the proliferation of spatial light modulators, digital holography is
finding wide-spread use in fields from augmented reality to medical imaging to
additive manufacturing to lithography to optical tweezing to
telecommunications. There are numerous types of SLM available with a multitude
of algorithms for generating holograms. Each algorithm has limitations in terms
of convergence speed, power efficiency, accuracy and data storage requirement.
  Here, we consider probably the most common algorithm for computer generated
holography - Gerchberg-Saxton - and examine the trade-off in convergent
quality, performance and efficiency. In particular, we focus on measuring and
understanding the factors that control runtime and convergence.
evaluation_method: reconstruction_error (MSE) along with convergence speed and runtime/performance metrics (e.g., iterations-to-convergence, power/efficiency)
general_score_metric: mean squared error (MSE) / reconstruction fidelity plus runtime/convergence statistics
reputation: Gerchberg–Saxton is the canonical baseline algorithm in computational holography and is widely used as a reference in optics and holography research.
notes: Non-LLM, domain-specific benchmark; results are hardware- and SLM-dependent (runtime and efficiency vary with device), and comparisons require consistent optical constraints and initialization; primarily a methodological/algorithmic benchmark rather than a large public dataset.
